E10.found_by: conformance lane, CONFORMANCE_AUDIT_V1, verified route by route
E10.v3_said: REFERENCE_IMPLEMENTED; residual: fronting with a hardened production server
E10.what_was_wrong: The GAP_LEDGER falsifier is defeated, but API_AND_OBSERVATORY.md is also part of the specification and 10 of its 12 named routes returned 404; query strings were not stripped from the path segment; every mutation is specified to return a StateTransitionReceipt on every outcome and the service returned ad-hoc dicts; and the service kept its own in-memory snapshot state, never touching the real store. V3's named residual (TLS, rate limits) named none of this.

E18.found_by: conformance lane, cross-referenced against HOSTILE_TEST_MATRIX.md row by row
E18.what_was_wrong: The 12 executed cases attack 7 of the matrix's 30 rows fully and 4 partially; 19 rows were never executed. The campaign's own docstring is honest -- it freezes its own list and never claims to be the matrix -- but V3 cited it as E18 closure. Worse, the campaign numbered its cases H01..H12, colliding with the matrix namespace while attacking different things: campaign H01 is stale-snapshot mutation, matrix H01 is kill during canonical blob write. A reader cross-referencing would conclude the wrong thing.

E3.found_by: restore lane, CROSS_PLANE_ATTACKS_V1 X11 and X12, confirmed in source
E3.what_was_wrong: SqliteAtlasPlaneStore.commit_batch had no compare-and-swap against the stored revision (base_atlas_revision was stored and never compared; expected_atlas_revision was recomputed from the same batch, a self-consistency check not a CAS) and no monotonic sequence check. The semantic store, which the atlas docstring claims to mirror, does both. A stale-base batch and a sequence-rewind batch both committed.

E4.what_was_wrong: Citation defect, not an overclaim. The fibre is supported, but the cited symbol is a runtime decision function; the thing that actually persists is engineering_control_store.SqliteControlProjectionStore.
